pages.text:
Robin Wilson wants to join Pi Beta Alpha, the exclusive club at Sweet Valley High. Elizabeth Wakefield nominates her, but Jessica and her friends object and try to keep Robin outside their circle. The disagreement puts the twins on opposite sides of a struggle over popularity and acceptance.

Kate William follows the pressure to fit in through school friendships and the prejudice directed at Robin. This Sweet Valley High story explores how a social group can turn belonging into a test, and what it costs to challenge the people setting its rules.

pages.title: Basic econometrics
pages.author: Damodar N. Gujarati

sourceEvidence.method: Publisher/catalogue records reviewed in web search and/or opened pages; ISBN, title, author and language matched. No raw API response is implied.
sourceEvidence.notes: Fourth-edition identity checked in university catalogues; chapter subjects cross-checked in university syllabuses specifying Gujarati and Sangeetha, fourth edition.

pages.text:
This fourth edition of Basic Econometrics, by Damodar N. Gujarati with Sangeetha, introduces the statistical methods used to investigate economic relationships. Regression provides the starting point: readers move from estimating a relationship between two variables to testing hypotheses and interpreting models with several explanatory variables.

The discussion also examines what happens when a model’s assumptions fail, including correlated errors and unequal error variance. It is a methods textbook for learning how economic claims are tested with data, with attention to the conditions that make those tests meaningful.

pages.title: The Cambridge History of Warfare
pages.author: Geoffrey Parker

sourceEvidence.method: Publisher/catalogue records reviewed in web search and/or opened pages; ISBN, title, author and language matched. No raw API response is implied.

pages.text:
Geoffrey Parker brings together military historians to examine the development of warfare in the West, from classical Greece and Rome through medieval and modern conflicts. The chapters connect changes in armies and weapons with the societies and resources that sustain them.

Published in 2005, this edition asks how particular forms of military organisation contributed to Western power. Its broad historical argument offers more than a sequence of battles, while remaining a study with a specific geographical perspective and a publication date that sets the limits of its contemporary coverage.

pages.title: Story
pages.author: Robert McKee

sourceEvidence.method: Publisher/catalogue records reviewed in web search and/or opened pages; ISBN, title, author and language matched. No raw API response is implied.

pages.text:
Robert McKee develops the ideas from his storytelling seminars into a guide to constructing narratives for the screen, stage and page. Story examines how a writer’s choices about structure, character and the unfolding of events work together, asking what makes an audience follow and care about a story.

The book approaches writing as a craft whose principles can be studied and applied. Its focus is the relationship between the parts of a narrative, making it useful to readers who want to analyse a draft as well as those preparing to write one.

pages.title: Seksuele gezondheid in Nederland 2006
pages.author: Floor Bakker

sourceEvidence.method: Publisher/catalogue records reviewed in web search and/or opened pages; ISBN, title, author and language matched. No raw API response is implied.

pages.text:
Deze onderzoeksbundel, onder redactie van Floor Bakker en Ine Vanwesenbeeck, brengt de seksuele gezondheid van Nederlanders van 19 tot 70 jaar in kaart. Het bevolkingsonderzoek behandelt onder meer relaties, anticonceptie, vruchtbaarheid, soa’s en de behoefte aan professionele hulp. Ook seksuele problemen en ervaringen met seksueel geweld krijgen aandacht.

De uitkomsten geven een beeld van de Nederlandse situatie rond 2006. Daarmee is het boek vooral bruikbaar als onderzoeksbron over die periode en als vertrekpunt voor vergelijking met later onderzoek naar gezondheid, zorggebruik en maatschappelijke veranderingen.

pages.title: Tilly
pages.author: Frank E. Peretti

sourceEvidence.method: Publisher/catalogue records reviewed in web search and/or opened pages; ISBN, title, author and language matched. No raw API response is implied.

pages.text:
Een echtpaar wordt opnieuw geconfronteerd met een abortus van negen jaar eerder. Wat in hun gezamenlijke verleden verborgen bleef, vraagt alsnog om woorden en een manier om verder te leven. Frank E. Peretti benadert die confrontatie vanuit een uitgesproken christelijke visie op vergeving.

Tilly is een korte roman over geloof, herinnering en de betekenis die de personages aan hun verleden geven. De Nederlandse vertaling van Petra van Eldik-Neleman verscheen bij Merweboek. De nadruk ligt op hun innerlijke en religieuze zoektocht, niet op een medisch of maatschappelijk overzicht van abortus.

Sara heeft in Dublin een leven opgebouwd wanneer haar vroegere vriendin Lejla na jaren weer contact zoekt. Ze vraagt Sara terug te komen naar Mostar en met haar op zoek te gaan naar haar verdwenen broer Armin. Tijdens hun reis naar Wenen komt ook de geschiedenis van hun vriendschap opnieuw in beweging.

pages.title: Overdressed
pages.author: Elizabeth L. Cline

sourceEvidence.method: Publisher/catalogue records reviewed in web search and/or opened pages; ISBN, title, author and language matched. No raw API response is implied.

pages.text:
Elizabeth L. Cline investigates what happens when clothing becomes cheap enough to buy almost without thinking. Following the path from production to crowded wardrobes and discarded garments, she connects everyday shopping habits with working conditions, environmental costs and the changing economics of fashion.

Overdressed asks readers to look beyond the price on a label and consider how clothes are made, used and valued. Its reporting also explores more deliberate ways of buying and caring for garments, making the relationship between personal consumption and the wider industry central to the book.

pages.title: Democratizing innovation
pages.author: Eric von Hippel

sourceEvidence.method: Publisher/catalogue records reviewed in web search and/or opened pages; ISBN, title, author and language matched. No raw API response is implied.

pages.text:
Eric von Hippel examines innovation that begins with the people using a product rather than with its manufacturer. Users adapt equipment and services to solve problems they know firsthand, then sometimes share their improvements freely. Examples range from sporting equipment and medical tools to software.

Democratizing Innovation considers how these activities change the roles of companies, user communities and public policy. It explains why knowledge held by users can be difficult for a producer to obtain, and how organisations might support that knowledge instead of treating innovation as an exclusively internal process.

pages.title: A History of American Architecture
pages.author: Mark Gelernter

sourceEvidence.method: Publisher/catalogue records reviewed in web search and/or opened pages; ISBN, title, author and language matched. No raw API response is implied.

pages.text:
Mark Gelernter traces American architecture through the cultural conditions that shaped it. Moving chronologically from early building traditions to the late twentieth century, he connects architectural choices with changing technologies, social ideas and influences arriving from Europe.

The book treats buildings as part of a wider history rather than as isolated examples of style. Its ten chapters provide a framework for comparing different periods and asking why particular forms became persuasive at particular moments. The historical survey extends to 1998, giving this edition a defined endpoint.

pages.title: The discovery of poetry
pages.author: Frances Mayes

sourceEvidence.method: Publisher/catalogue records reviewed in web search and/or opened pages; ISBN, title, author and language matched. No raw API response is implied.

pages.text:
Frances Mayes brings reading poetry and writing it into the same conversation. The Discovery of Poetry moves from the effects of individual words and images to rhythm, voice and poetic form, using poems alongside questions and writing exercises.

This second edition encourages readers to notice how a poem works before trying related choices in their own writing. Its concluding handbook turns to the creative process and revision. The result is both an introduction for readers who want more confidence with poetry and a practical companion for beginning poets.

pages.text:
Randall Collins uses sociology to question explanations that initially seem obvious. Everyday relationships, crime and the exercise of power become occasions to examine the social patterns behind individual behaviour. The aim is to show how a sociological argument can reveal connections that common sense misses.

This second edition presents those arguments through recognisable situations rather than treating society as a list of definitions. It invites readers to distinguish personal intentions from the structures and interactions around them, and to reconsider why familiar institutions work as they do.

Awsten Knight gathers personal stories and reflections on relationships, self-acceptance and the difficult questions that remain after painful experiences. Known as the singer of Waterparks, he brings the attention usually directed at his music into an autobiographical account of the person behind it.

You’d Be Paranoid Too (If Everyone Was Out to Get You) moves between intimate memories and observations about dealing with other people. Its perspective is personal rather than a guide to psychological treatment, offering readers an extended encounter with Knight’s experiences and voice.

pages.text:
David Hughes follows the kings and queens of Britain through ancient traditions, Roman rule, the early medieval kingdoms and the Norman succession. This first volume arranges the material as a chronicle of royal houses, with chapters on Arthurian Britain, Anglo-Saxon rulers and the Viking period.

The account places legendary beginnings alongside recorded history and discusses alternative interpretations of disputed evidence. Readers interested in dynasties and succession should distinguish those reconstructions from securely documented events. The genealogical charts are identified as a separate second volume, rather than part of this book.

pages.text:
After their adoptive father dies, Maia and her sisters return to the family home in Switzerland and receive clues to their origins. Maia’s search leads her to Rio de Janeiro, where the history of another family opens a route into her own.

Lucinda Riley links this present-day investigation with Izabela’s life in the 1920s and a journey to Paris connected with the creation of Christ the Redeemer. The first Seven Sisters novel combines a search for ancestry with an earlier story of love, ambition and choices whose consequences reach across generations.

pages.sourceName: Princeton University Press — Part II overview
pages.text:
This edition contains the second volume of Søren Kierkegaard’s Either/Or. Judge William addresses the younger man whose outlook shapes the first volume, arguing for a life formed through ethical choice, commitment and responsibility. Marriage becomes one of the central subjects through which that position is explored.

Kierkegaard presents the argument through a distinctive fictional voice rather than a detached summary of philosophical doctrines. The tension between immediate experience and sustained commitment remains open to the reader’s judgment. This volume should be read as one side of the larger work’s conversation.

Five years after her relationship with Logan Sutherland ended, Fiona faces him again when he discovers that she has a son he knew nothing about. Logan demands a marriage, and Fiona considers agreeing for Jonathan’s sake while resisting the expectations that come with it.

Robyn Donald’s romance places an unresolved past inside an uneasy family arrangement. Fiona’s determination to protect her child is complicated by her feelings for Logan, making the distance between a practical agreement and a trusting relationship the central conflict.

pages.text:
Ayla lives with Jondalar and their daughter Jonayla among the Zelandonii while undertaking the demanding training of a spiritual leader. Visits to sacred caves introduce her to paintings and rituals that deepen her understanding of the people around her, but the time devoted to learning also strains family life.

The sixth Earth’s Children novel concludes Jean M. Auel’s prehistoric saga. It combines the practical demands of food, travel and healing with Ayla’s search for knowledge, following the consequences when her responsibilities as a learner, partner and mother pull in different directions.

A history lesson becomes a classroom experiment in discipline and group identity. As students adopt its routines and slogans, the sense of belonging begins to turn into pressure on anyone who questions the group. Laurie sees friends changing around her and tries to persuade their teacher to stop.

Todd Strasser’s novel dramatises a real classroom experiment to explore the attraction of authoritarian ideas. The school setting brings its questions close to everyday experience: how easily loyalty becomes obedience, and how difficult it can be to challenge a movement supported by your friends.

Nadine leidt in Brabant een cateringbedrijf wanneer ze de succesvolle ontwerper Daniel ontmoet. Zijn aantrekkingskracht en luxueuze wereld maken indruk, maar naarmate hun verhouding intenser wordt, verliest ze steeds meer houvast in haar eigen leven. De vraag wat zij zelf wil, wordt daardoor moeilijker los te zien van zijn invloed.

De ontmoeting opent de erotische romanreeks Muren van glas van Marique Maas. Het verhaal draait om verlangen en de machtsverhouding binnen een nieuwe relatie, waarin Nadine probeert te begrijpen of haar gevoelens verder reiken dan de aantrekkingskracht van het moment.

pages.text:
Zayn looks back on leaving One Direction and beginning a solo career in a book that combines personal writing with photographs, drawings and notes. The transition to Mind of Mine provides a setting for reflections on music, fame and the difficulty of defining yourself under public scrutiny.

Published in 2016, this autobiography takes the form of a visual scrapbook as well as a written account. It gives the artist’s own perspective on that particular stage of his life, with private memories and creative materials placed beside the public story of his career.

pages.author: Mary Otto

pages.beforeSynopsis: Teeth takes readers on a disturbing journey into America's silent epidemic of oral disease, exposing the hidden connections between tooth decay and stunted job prospects, low educational achievement, social mobility, and the troubling state of our public health.
pages.sourceName: National Association of Science Writers — Mary Otto on her book
pages.text:
Mary Otto begins with the death of Deamonte Driver, a child whose untreated dental infection became fatal, and investigates the barriers that keep people in the United States from receiving dental care. Her reporting follows patients and the system they must navigate, connecting oral health with income, insurance and the organisation of dentistry.

Teeth combines the history of a profession with accounts of unequal access to treatment. The book asks why something as personal as a smile can reveal so much about social position and the distribution of healthcare.

pages.text:
Photographs make it appear that Sharley and Marcos Santana are having an affair, threatening a business merger and already tense relations at his Portuguese vineyards. To remove their value as blackmail, the pair agree to marry, intending the arrangement to exist in name only.

Rachel Lindsay’s romance follows the complications of that hurried solution. Marcos’s relationship with Teresa and the feelings stirred by the marriage make a supposedly practical agreement increasingly difficult to contain. The story turns on the gap between what the photographs suggest and what the people involved actually want.

edition.by_statement: Shirley Jackson ; introduction by Patrick McGrath.

description.value:
A haunting and powerful collection of stories from one of America's finest writers, with a new Introduction by Patrick McGrath.

Eerie, unforgettable, and by turns terrifying and hilarious, Shirley Jackson's collection of stories plunges us into a unique, brilliantly etched world where the uncanny lurks in the everyday and where nothing is quite what it seems. In "The Lottery," Jackson's most famous work and one of the greatest--and scariest--stories of the twentieth century, a small town gathers for an annual ritual that culminates in a terrible event. In "The Daemon Lover," a woman waits, then searches, for the man she is to marry that day, only to find that he has disappeared as completely as if he had never existed. In "Trial by Combat," a shy woman confronts her kleptomaniac neighbor, and in "Pillar of Salt," a tourist in New York is gradually paralyzed by a city grown nightmarish. Throughout these twenty-five tales, we move through a variety of emotional landscapes full of loneliness and humor, oddity and cruelty, banality and terror, and searing psychological insight. No reader will come away unaffected.

The only collection to appear during Jackson's lifetime, The Lottery and Other Stories reveals the full breadth and power of this truly original writer.
(jacket)

pages.text:
A village prepares for its annual ritual, a woman searches for her vanished fiancé, and a visitor finds New York increasingly impossible to navigate. In these stories, Shirley Jackson makes ordinary social encounters and familiar places become sources of unease.

The collection includes The Lottery, The Daemon Lover and Pillar of Salt, bringing together psychological dread, cruelty and dark humour. This Modern Library edition includes an introduction by Patrick McGrath. Across the stories, the unsettling effect often comes from watching everyday expectations continue after something has gone profoundly wrong.

pages.author: Delphine de Vigan

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Loading the description. Lou Bertignac is thirteen, with an IQ of 160. At home her father hides his sadness, while her mother, after the death of her second child, barely speaks. Lou escapes by frequenting Paris's Gare d'Austerlitz; observing the emotional scenes amid the arrivals and departures.
There she meets No, a homeless girl, and makes her the subject of her class project. Then No disappears, leaving Lou devastated. However, when Lou's parents agree to let No come to live with them, she sets out to bring her up to the light of a home and a family life. Or so she believes.
pages.text:
Lou Bertignac’s school project brings her into contact with No, a teenager living on the streets of Paris. Their conversations become a friendship, and Lou asks her parents to let No move into the family home. The decision also exposes the sadness and silence already present there.

Delphine de Vigan follows Lou’s wish to help as it meets circumstances that friendship alone cannot easily resolve. Translated into English by George Miller, No and Me connects a young person’s growing awareness of homelessness with questions about family, care and the limits of good intentions.

pages.sourceName: Wake County Public Libraries — edition and synopsis
pages.text:
On Okinawa in 1945, fourteen-year-old Hideki is drawn into the fighting and ordered to kill American soldiers, although his own concern is finding his family. Across the island, Ray faces his first battle as a young American Marine. Each has been taught to fear the people on the other side.

Alan Gratz brings their paths together in a novel about young people caught in war. The alternating perspectives expose the difference between an enemy imagined from a distance and a frightened person encountered face to face, making individual choices central to the larger conflict.

pages.text:
Hakim reist met zijn zusje Sita en hun moeder in een luchtschip. Een lastige passagier dwingt hen naar Endar te vliegen, een planeet waar computers een oorlog blijven uitvechten. Zo komt hun reis terecht in een omgeving die door dat voortdurende conflict wordt bepaald.

Tais Teng schrijft dit sciencefictionverhaal voor jonge lezers in korte zinnen en met eenvoudige woorden. Door het dode land verscheen in de reeks Zoeklicht, met tekeningen van Fred Marschall. Het combineert een avontuur op een vreemde planeet met een toegankelijke manier van vertellen.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Loading the description. Harry August is on his deathbed. Again. No matter what he does or the decisions he makes, when death comes, Harry always returns to where he began, a child with all the knowledge of a life he has already lived a dozen times before. Nothing ever changes. Until now.
As Harry nears the end of his eleventh life, a little girl appears at his bedside. 'I nearly missed you, Doctor August, ' she says. 'I need to send a message.' This is the story of what Harry does next, and what he did before, and how he tries to save a past he cannot change and a future he cannot allow.
pages.text:
Whenever Harry August dies, he returns to the beginning of the same life with his memories intact. Repetition gives him knowledge that other people cannot share, but at the end of his eleventh life a young visitor brings a message that changes what those returns mean.

Claire North builds a mystery around a man who can revisit his own history while carrying the consequences of earlier choices. Friendship, betrayal and the possibility of an altered future turn his unusual experience of time into a problem that reaches beyond his own survival.
